Write an email to a colleague about thanking a team after a big launch. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Thank you for getting us over the line

Hi all,

Yesterday we launched the new service to the public, and I want to start with the most important thing: thank you. It's been astonishing to watch this come together.

Eighteen months ago, this was a set of ambitions and a rather optimistic slide deck. Today, real people are using it to do something that used to take them weeks, and they are doing it in a matter of minutes. That is entirely down to the work of this team.

Let me be specific about what I'm proud of, because it deserves more than a general round of applause.

First, the way you worked together. Developers, designers, user researchers, policy colleagues and the operations team sat in the same conversations, argued openly and then agreed a way forward. Siloed approaches rarely survive contact with real users, and you didn't let one take hold here. When the research showed that our first design wasn't working, nobody dug in. You changed it, and the service is much better for it.

Second, the way you handled the hard weeks. The final month was not easy. We had a late change to the security requirements, a supplier delay and a tight window for testing. Each time, you stayed calm, said clearly what you needed and helped each other out. Several of you gave up evenings and weekends, and I know that wasn't a small ask. Please take the time back. I mean that, and I will back you up with your managers if anyone needs persuading.

Third, the quality of what we have built. It is open, it is accessible and it is built on foundations that other teams can reuse. That matters. We should never have to reinvent the wheel every single time we build something new, and thanks to you, the next team won't have to.

I should be clear that launch is a beginning, not an end. We now have the chance to watch how people use the service, fix what isn't working and keep improving it. Over the coming weeks I'd like us to share what we've learned, both the things that went well and the things we would do differently, so that others across the organisation can benefit.

For now, though, please enjoy this. There's cake in the kitchen on Thursday afternoon, and I'd love it if as many of you as possible could come along so that I can say thank you in person.

If there's anything you need from me, or anything you think I could have done better, don't hesitate to get in touch. I'm counting on your help for what comes next.

With sincere thanks,

[name]
